short: Egypt's imperial phase, when the Nile kingdom ruled from Nubia to the Euphrates.
full:
Ahmose I expelled the Hyksos rulers of the Delta around 1550 BCE and founded the Eighteenth Dynasty, which Egyptologists take as the start of the New Kingdom. For the next five centuries Egypt was an aggressive territorial power rather than a self-contained river state. Thutmose III campaigned in the Levant seventeen times, Hatshepsut sent fleets to Punt, Akhenaten moved capital and cult to Amarna, and Ramesses II fought the Hittites to a draw at Kadesh in 1274 BCE before signing the earliest international peace treaty to survive.

The Twentieth Dynasty faced raids by the Sea Peoples, grain inflation, systematic robbery of the royal tombs, and the first recorded strike, by the workmen of Deir el-Medina under Ramesses III. Real power drifted to the High Priests of Amun at Thebes. The period is conventionally closed at about 1069 BCE with the death of Ramesses XI, after which Egypt was divided between rulers at Tanis and Thebes for four hundred years.
